title: Prompt-length conditioned KV-cache miss pathology and per-stage quantile breakdown
content:
Summary:
This is a working investigation into an observed tail-latency mode that correlates strongly with prompt length and KV-cache miss patterns on the inference serving nodes. The behavior manifests as a p99 spike depending on the number of preserved prefix tokens and an increased incidence of asynchronous cache refills during streaming. This doc captures the sampling approach, per-stage quantile breakdowns, representative traces, hypotheses, and next-step experiments.

Context / motivation:
- Regression surfaced in CUSTOMER-A telemetry (INF-3421) — sharp increase in p99 for chat sessions with long contexts (>1024 tokens).
- Console dashboards show stable p50/p95 but growing p99 over last 3 weeks after a runtime change that adjusted KV cache sharding heuristics and added dynamic quantization selection.
- We want reproducible trace-level evidence to decide whether to roll back heuristics or implement targeted mitigations (prefetching, stronger batching caps, or bypass mode).

Hardware & software baseline used for measurements:
- Instance: rxi.gpu-16 (A300 analog), 8 GPUs per host, single-worker per GPU config used in test harness.
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.13.2 (PR 987 partially in prod canary).
- Model: open-llama-13B-4bit (fp4-like quant profile), KV-cache enabled with LRU sharding across GPU memory.
- Load generator: local weighted-rps replay from production traces (sampled, anonymized).
- Sampling window: 3 hours, ~120k requests, mixture: 70% chat-short (<128 tokens), 20% medium (128–1024), 10% long (>1024).

Sampling & trace selection:
- We capture full e2e traces including these logical stages: ingress-auth, router-decision, enqueue-batch, batch-wait, kv-lookup, kv-async-refill, model-forward, postprocess, egress-stream.
- To focus on pathological tails we select traces where total_time >= 95th percentile of each prompt-length bucket, then further cluster by the largest contributing stage.
- We also pull contiguous long-session traces for a smaller set of sessions to inspect temporal correlation across tokens.

Aggregate quantiles (all traffic mixture):
- total_e2e: p50=43ms, p95=131ms, p99=382ms
- model_forward: p50=28ms, p95=80ms, p99=210ms
- batch_wait: p50=1ms, p95=6ms, p99=47ms
- kv_lookup: p50=2ms, p95=8ms, p99=60ms
- kv_async_refill (when present): p50=0ms, p95=42ms, p99=220ms
- router + auth: p50=1ms, p95=3ms, p99=12ms
- egress_stream: p50=0ms, p95=5ms, p99=28ms

Breakdown by prompt-length bucket (important differences):
1) Short (<128 tokens) — 78% of requests in sample
   - total: p50=36ms, p95=98ms, p99=210ms
   - model_forward p99 dominates ~65% of tail traces (heavy seqlen compute but KV hits good)
2) Medium (128–1024) — 18%
   - total: p50=67ms, p95=165ms, p99=420ms
   - kv_lookup p99 and kv_async_refill appear in ~30% of medium tail traces
3) Long (>1024) — 4% (but outsized tail contribution)
   - total: p50=140ms, p95=410ms, p99=1180ms
   - kv_async_refill present in ~62% of p99 traces; when refill coincides with batch boundary we see amplification (refill + model_forward serialized)

Representative trace archetypes (extracted raw timelines):
- Case A: KV miss with synchronous refill (medium prompt)  -> enqueue-batch 3ms | batch-wait 45ms | kv-lookup 6ms | kv_async_refill 130ms | model_forward 78ms | post 12ms => total 274ms
- Case B: Cold-start model-forward (short prompt, GPU warmup)  -> enqueue 1ms | batch-wait 60ms | model_forward 210ms | post 8ms => total 280ms
- Case C: Long prompt, repeated async refills across tokens  -> repeated small kv_async_refill events interleaved with model_forward; p99 dominated by sum of many small refills + occasional stall on refill completion => total 1.1s+

Initial triage & hypotheses (ranked):
1) Heuristic regression: new KV sharding heuristic increases inter-GPU cache misses for longer prefixes, causing async refill storms. Evidence: elevated kv_async_refill counts in canary nodes after PR 987.
2) Dynamic quantization selection increases model_forward variance for certain sequence shapes (noted as higher model_forward p99 in short-batch coldstarts).
3) Batching boundaries align with refill completion causing serialization: when a refill completes just before the model starts, refill processing can block compute path for that batch on some runtimes.
4) A rare scheduler starvation path in worker event loop (SRE issue noted) that surfaces only under high-token sessions.

Quick checks we ran (results):
- Canary vs baseline comparison (A/B): Canary p99 total increased by ~28% for medium+long buckets; kv_async_refill incidents up 3.6x.
- Instrumented per-GPU refill counters: confirmed higher cross-GPU refill traffic on canary.
- Micro-replay: replayed a single long session against baseline vs canary — canary produced repeated async refills that baseline did not.

Immediate mitigations considered (fast rollbacks / config knobs):
- Roll back KV sharding heuristic to previous stable (INF-3421-hotfix) — expected to reduce cross-GPU miss rate; risk: increased memory fragmentation.
- Introduce a soft cap: throttle async refill concurrency per host (e.g., max 2 concurrent refills) to avoid refill storms; tradeoff: higher steady-state miss latency but fewer p99 spikes.
- Pre-warm strategy: prefetch KV for sessions that exceed a prompt-length threshold (costly for short sessions).

Planned experiments (next 7 days):
1) Controlled A/B with a synthetic traffic mix that amplifies long sessions (50% long) to verify linearity of refill amplification (owner: Ethan; ticket INF-3479).
2) Deploy refill-concurrency throttle in staging and measure p99 movement (owner: Marta; PR: draft in /prs/1002).
3) Run model-forward variance sweep with and without dynamic quant selection to isolate that factor (owner: Diego).
4) Add a sampling hook to trace which GPU was the authoritative owner of KV shards at time of miss to see cross-host vs intra-host patterns.

Observability gaps & suggested additions:
- We need a per-request KV-origin field in trace (cache_hit|local_miss|remote_miss) to quickly classify traces without offline correlation.
- Add per-host refill concurrency gauge to the console and an alert when refill_concurrent > 4 for >30s.
- Histogram views for refill duration (not just count) by prompt-length bucket.

Decisions for short-term action (proposal to ship by EOD):
- Enable refill-concurrency throttle in canary (staging validated) and keep PR 987 canary running; measure p99s for 48h. (Owner: Marta)
- Create rollback plan for KV sharding heuristic with a runbook and communication for Dedicated customers in case we need immediate revert. (Owner: Priya)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do medium prompts sometimes exhibit a higher refill penalty than long prompts in some runs? (sampling skew or different batching interactions?)
- Is there any pathological interaction with the streaming encoder that increases chance of refill occurring mid-batch?
- Are autoscaling bursts causing transient eviction of shards that then trigger refills?

Notes to self / rough todo list:
- Attach sample traces (exported pcap-like JSON) to INF-3421 (Ethan).
- Schedule 30m sync with model infra + storage owners to review sharding assumptions (invite list: priya, ethan, marta, diego).
- Draft rollback announcement for Dedicated contacts if we decide to revert the heuristic.

Appendix: quick ascii quantile table (all in ms)
| bucket | p50 | p95 | p99 | top-stage-in-p99 |
| short  | 36  | 98  | 210 | model_forward     |
| medium | 67  | 165 | 420 | kv_async_refill   |
| long   | 140 | 410 | 1180| kv_async_refill   |

If you want more raw traces or the small replay harness used locally, say the word and I will drop the shell commands and trace artifacts into INF-3421/attachments.

-- Priya
